cases.prompt: Our team does the same monthly list check in every region and each one does it a bit differently. I think this should become one of our skills. Where do I start?
cases.expected_output: Starts by searching the registry for an existing skill and naming an owner. Says to mine the department record before general knowledge. Asks for a one-page brief agreed by the owner before writing. Mentions three test cases. Does not mark anything reviewed or verified.

cases.prompt: One of our skills got a C in the quality check and people say it is vague. How do we fix it properly?
cases.expected_output: Points to the gates in order and the findings table. Warns against adding text only to please the checker. Asks for a worked example, a pitfalls list and a description with a not-for boundary. Keeps status draft and leaves review to the owner.

cases.prompt: Please make a new skill about how to score a business case. We have no owner for it yet but it should be quick.
cases.expected_output: Notes that a skill for this topic may already exist and asks to check the registry. Refuses to proceed without a named owner. Says extend the existing skill instead of adding a second one.

cases.prompt: Write me a short note summarising yesterday's workshop for the plant team.
cases.expected_output: Recognises this is a one-off note, not a skill. Does not run the authoring method or the scaffold script.

should_trigger: How do I turn this recurring OD procedure into a skill for the registry?
Our skill was rated below B, how do we improve it?
Scaffold a new skill folder and tell me what the registry entry should look like.
What are the gates a new skill has to pass before the pull request?
should_not_trigger: Write a prompt that summarises my meeting notes.
Update the business case skill with the new savings figures from the plant.
Which skill decides whether a request is accepted into a lane?
Create a PowerPoint deck about our skills.
